Problem: A point has rectangular coordinates $(2,-1,-2)$ and spherical coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi).$  Find the rectangular coordinates of the point with spherical coordinates $(\rho, \theta, 2 \phi).$

message.content:
Using the standard spherical-coordinate convention
\[
x=\rho\sin\phi\cos\theta,\quad y=\rho\sin\phi\sin\theta,\quad z=\rho\cos\phi,
\]
we first find \(\rho,\theta,\phi\) from \((2,-1,-2)\).

\[
\rho=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+(-2)^2}=\sqrt{9}=3.
\]
Since \(z=\rho\cos\phi=-2\),
\[
\cos\phi=-\frac23,\qquad \sin\phi=\sqrt{1-\frac49}=\frac{\sqrt5}{3}.
\]
Also,
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{x}{\rho\sin\phi}=\frac{2}{3\cdot \sqrt5/3}=\frac{2}{\sqrt5},
\]
\[
\sin\theta=\frac{y}{\rho\sin\phi}=\frac{-1}{\sqrt5}.
\]

Now compute functions of \(2\phi\):
\[
\cos 2\phi=\cos^2\phi-\sin^2\phi=\frac49-\frac59=-\frac19,
\]
\[
\sin 2\phi=2\sin\phi\cos\phi=2\cdot \frac{\sqrt5}{3}\cdot\left(-\frac23\right)=-\frac{4\sqrt5}{9}.
\]

For spherical coordinates \((\rho,\theta,2\phi)=(3,\theta,2\phi)\):
\[
x'=\rho\sin(2\phi)\cos\theta
=3\left(-\frac{4\sqrt5}{9}\right)\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt5}\right)
=-\frac83,
\]
\[
y'=\rho\sin(2\phi)\sin\theta
=3\left(-\frac{4\sqrt5}{9}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt5}\right)
=\frac43,
\]
\[
z'=\rho\cos(2\phi)=3\left(-\frac19\right)=-\frac13.
\]

The answer is \(\left(-\frac83,\frac43,-\frac13\right)\).
